| Supported | The **GeForce RTX 30 series** is a suite of [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit "Graphics processing unit") (GPUs) developed by [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia"), succeeding the [GeForce RTX 20 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_20_series "GeForce RTX 20 series"). The GeForce RTX 30 series is based on the [Ampere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampere_\(microarchitecture\) "Ampere \(microarchitecture\)") architecture, which features Nvidia's second-generation [ray tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_tracing_\(graphics\)#Interactive_ray_tracing "Ray tracing \(graphics\)") (RT) cores and third-generation [Tensor Cores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning_super_sampling#Architecture "Deep learning super sampling").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-4) Part of the [Nvidia RTX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_RTX "Nvidia RTX") series, [hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray-tracing_hardware "Ray-tracing hardware")-enabled [real-time ray tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_ray_tracing "Real-time ray tracing") is featured on GeForce RTX 30 series cards. The lineup was designed to compete with [AMD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Micro_Devices "Advanced Micro Devices")'s [Radeon RX 6000 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radeon_RX_6000_series "Radeon RX 6000 series") of cards. It consists of the entry-level (and previously laptop-exclusive) RTX 3050 and laptop-exclusive RTX 3050 Ti, the mid-range RTX 3060, the upper-midrange RTX 3060 Ti and RTX 3070, the high-end RTX 3070 Ti, RTX 308010GB, and RTX 308012GB, the laptop-exclusive RTX 3080 16GB, and the enthusiast-class RTX 3080 Ti, RTX 3090, and RTX 3090 Ti. This was the last generation from Nvidia to have official support for Windows 7, as the latest drivers available for this generation require at least Windows 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-6) The GeForce RTX 30 series began shipping on September 17, 2020.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-7)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-geforceSpecialEvent-8) The initial launch, consisting of the RTX 3070, RTX 3080, and RTX 3090, occurred during the [2020–2023 global chip shortage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_chip_shortage_\(2020%E2%80%932023\) "Global chip shortage \(2020–2023\)"), resulting in widespread and notable shortages of the series as a whole that lasted from the series' launch until 2022. The GeForce RTX 30 series was succeeded by the [GeForce RTX 40 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series "GeForce RTX 40 series"), powered by the [Ada Lovelace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace_\(microarchitecture\) "Ada Lovelace \(microarchitecture\)") microarchitecture, which first launched in 2022.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-9) ## Release and availability issues [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Release and availability issues")] See also: [2020–2023 global chip shortage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%932023_global_chip_shortage "2020–2023 global chip shortage") Launch day for the RTX 3080 was September 17, 2020.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:1-10) The lack of pre-order functionality and high demand exacerbated by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), and boost in scalping, resulted in a large number of online retailers struggling with the sheer number of purchases.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:1-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-11) [Newegg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newegg "Newegg") had completely sold out as expected on [Black Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Friday_\(shopping\) "Black Friday \(shopping\)"). Long lines formed outside physical stores with stock, such as [Micro Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro_Center "Micro Center") in the United States,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-12) and [Dospara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirdwave_Group?action=edit&redlink=1 "Thirdwave Group \(page does not exist\)")[[ja](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%B5%E3%83%BC%E3%83%89%E3%82%A6%E3%82%A7%E3%83%BC%E3%83%96 "ja:サードウェーブ")] in Japan.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-13) Twitter users reported that they used bots to buy large numbers of cards to resell for higher prices.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:2-14) Nvidia released a statement the following day, apologizing for the difficulties with their online store, which went down on launch day due to high traffic.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-15) On October 2, Nvidia announced that it would delay the release of RTX 3070 cards by two weeks to guarantee availability.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-16) On October 5, Nvidia CEO [Jensen Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jensen_Huang "Jensen Huang") announced delays due to supply shortages, which were expected to go on until 2021.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-17) On October 9, the company announced that all Founder's Edition graphic cards in the United States would temporarily be sold via [Best Buy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy "Best Buy"), while the official web store would be upgraded to improve the shopping experience.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-20) In early December, Nvidia blamed continued component shortages on Samsung [wafer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wafer_\(electronics\) "Wafer \(electronics\)") shortages, resulting in [chip shortages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip_shortage "Chip shortage"), among other factors.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-21) Shortages of RTX 30 series cards continued throughout 2021[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-22) and well into 2022 [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-23). In an effort to limit purchases by crypto miners, Nvidia announced in February that the RTX 3060 cards would be able to detect algorithms for mining of the Ethereum cryptocurrency and halve the hash rate.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-24) Shortly after release, Nvidia accidentally released a driver update which disabled the detection.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-25) In March, TechRadar reported that the shortages could continue until the third quarter of the year, in part blaming a global GDDR6 memory shortage and the cards' supply being bought out by [cryptominers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency#Mining "Cryptocurrency").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-26) In April, [Hong Kong Customs and Excise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_Customs_and_Excise "Hong Kong Customs and Excise") seized 300 non-video CMP cards.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-27) Nvidia officially announced new RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX 3060 Ti Limited Hash Rate (LHR) SKUs on May 18, 2021, which limits the Ethereum hash mining hash rate.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-28) Nvidia released the RTX 3080 Ti on June 3, and the RTX 3070 Ti one week later, on June 10. Both included the cryptocurrency mining hash rate limiter.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-29) There have been multiple attempts to meet the demand. [EVGA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EVGA_Corporation "EVGA Corporation") introduced a system designed to put people into a queue, with the goal being to prevent cards from selling out quickly and decrease wait time.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-30) Besides the Founders Edition, there are also a variety of aftermarket cards, referred to as "custom cards" by Nvidia. The graphics chip is taken from Nvidia and parts of the card are modified according to the company's specifications. Such modifications include: clock speeds, fans, heat sinks, connectors, and aesthetics. Such aftermarket cards tend to perform better than Nvidia's in-house cards, but the increased performance comes with tradeoffs in temperature and power consumption. Manufacturers include [Gigabyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigabyte_Technology "Gigabyte Technology"), [MSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro-Star_International "Micro-Star International"), [ZOTAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZOTAC "ZOTAC"), [Asus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asus "Asus"), [EVGA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EVGA_Corporation "EVGA Corporation"), and INNO3D.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-31)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-35) Nvidia officially released the GeForce RTX 3080 12GB graphics card on January 11, 2022 and the desktop GeForce RTX 3050 graphics card on January 27, 2022. The RTX 3050 had previously only had a laptop variant that was launched on May 11, 2021, along with the laptop variant of the RTX 3050 Ti that currently still has no desktop variant. Nvidia officially released the GeForce RTX 3090 Ti on March 29, 2022. ## Details [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Details")] [![Bar chart comparing CUDA cores per USD \(blue bars, left y-axis\) and memory bandwidth per USD in GB/s \(orange bars, right y-axis\) across various NVIDIA GeForce RTX 30-series models. Models on x-axis range from RTX 3050 to RTX 3090 with corresponding prices, CUDA cores, and memory bandwidth listed below each bar group. The RTX 3080 model shows the highest CUDA cores per USD ratio, while memory bandwidth per USD peaks at the RTX 3060 Ti. Both metrics generally decrease for higher-end, more expensive models like the RTX 3080 Ti and RTX 3090. The chart illustrates cost-efficiency trade-offs in GPU performance components.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/CUDA_Cores_and_Memory_Bandwidth_per_USD_for_RTX_30-series.png/250px-CUDA_Cores_and_Memory_Bandwidth_per_USD_for_RTX_30-series.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CUDA_Cores_and_Memory_Bandwidth_per_USD_for_RTX_30-series.png)CUDA cores and memory bandwidth per USD for RTX 30-series GPUs Architectural improvements of the Ampere architecture include the following: * [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 8.6[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-36) * [Samsung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung_Electronics "Samsung Electronics") 8nm 8N (8LPH) process (custom designed for Nvidia)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-NVIDIA-ampere-GA102-37) * Doubled FP32 performance per SM on Ampere GPUs * Third-generation Tensor Cores with FP16, bfloat16, TensorFloat-32 (TF32) and sparsity acceleration * Second-generation Ray Tracing Cores, plus concurrent ray tracing and shading and compute * [GDDR6X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDDR6_SDRAM#GDDR6X "GDDR6 SDRAM") memory support (RTX 3060Ti GDDR6X Version, RTX 3070 Ti, RTX 3080, RTX 3080 12GB, RTX 3080 Ti, RTX 3090, RTX 3090 Ti) * [PCI Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCI_Express "PCI Express") 4.0 * [NVLink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVLink "NVLink") 3.0 (RTX 3090, RTX 3090 Ti) * [HDMI 2.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HDMI_2.1 "HDMI 2.1") supporting FRL6 (48Gbit/s) transmission speed[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-38) * [PureVideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_PureVideo "Nvidia PureVideo") Feature Set K hardware video decoding with [AV1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AV1 "AV1") hardware decoding[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-39)

However, the problem would be that the RTX 3090 offers similar performance while "it costs significantly less."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:3-97) In addition to its price, they criticized the RTX 3090 Ti's high power consumption.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:3-97) The performance was praised, as the 3090 Ti "will likely be the go-to GPU for creative professionals that need brute force in their day-to-day work." In gaming, "the RTX 3090 Ti fares quite a bit better" compared to the RTX 3090, and even in 8K "will be able to hit a solid 60 fps in many games at high settings."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:3-97) ### RTX 3090 [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: RTX 3090")] _[PC Gamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PC_Gamer "PC Gamer")_ described the Nvidia GeForce RTX 3090 as a "frankly enormous graphics card", which is "supremely powerful" and "more worthy of its Titan credentials than the GeForce branding", as for the average gamer "it doesn't deliver enough over the RTX 3080 to make sense, but for the pro-creator it's a workload-crushing card."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-98) ### RTX 3080 [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: RTX 3080")] _[GamesRadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar "GamesRadar")_ praised the RTX 3080 for its capability to "run almost any game at 4K60fps with [ray tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_tracing_\(graphics\) "Ray tracing \(graphics\)")" and found that it offers "4K gaming at an accessible price for the first time ever".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-99) According to _[The Verge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Verge "The Verge")_ , "4K gaming arrived with the RTX 2080 Ti", but "the RTX 3080 does the same and more at a much more affordable price point."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:0-100) Overall, the RTX 3080 would be "great for 1440p or 4K gaming"; however, they criticized the requirement of a 750W power supply as well as the 10GB of VRAM regarding future games.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-:0-100) ### RTX 3070 [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: RTX 3070")] Jim McGregor from _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ found that "the RTX 3070 is the perfect solution for the more mainstream gamer", while "the competitive gamer or high-end creator will still likely opt for the GeForce RTX 3080 or RTX 3090."[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-101) ## Support [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Support")] Nvidia transitioned driver support for the [Windows 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_7 "Windows 7") operating system to legacy status and stopped issuing new security drivers for this operating system in September 2024.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series#cite_note-102) The RTX 30 series is the last Nvidia GPU architecture to support the Windows 7 operating system; the RTX 40 and later series of GPUs require [Windows 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_10 "Windows 10") or later. ## See also [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_30_series&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: See also")] * [GeForce GTX 10 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_GTX_10_series "GeForce GTX 10 series") * [GeForce RTX 50 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_50_series "GeForce RTX 50 series") * [Quadro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadro "Quadro") * [Nvidia Tesla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_Tesla "Nvidia Tesla") * [List of Nvidia graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nvidia_graphics_processing_units "List of Nvidia graphics processing units")
